title: Back-of-the-envelope estimate helpers
problem: A design doc's numbers section answers 'how big is this?' before anyone picks Redis or Kafka. Write four small helpers that turn requirements into numbers: requests per second, storage, human-readable sizes, and whether reads need a cache. Read each docstring carefully: the rounding and the boundaries are part of the spec.
requirements: rps: average = requests_per_day / 86400 and peak = average * peak_factor, each rounded up with math.ceil; ValueError for negative traffic or peak_factor < 1
storage_bytes: rows * bytes * days * overhead, rounded up; ValueError for negative arguments or overhead < 1
human_bytes: 'N B' below 1000, otherwise one decimal in KB/MB/GB/TB (powers of 1000), never beyond TB
needs_cache: True only when peak reads are strictly above db capacity * headroom
contract:
rps(requests_per_day: int, peak_factor: float) -> tuple[int, int]
storage_bytes(rows_per_day: int, bytes_per_row: int, days: int, overhead: float = 1.0) -> int
human_bytes(n: int) -> str
needs_cache(peak_read_rps: float, db_read_capacity_rps: float, headroom: float = 0.5) -> bool
edgeCases: Tiny traffic (1 request/day) rounds up to 1 rps, zero stays 0
Exact values aren't rounded up further (86,400/day is exactly 1 rps)
Beyond TB stays in TB (5000.0 TB)
Peak exactly at the headroom limit doesn't need a cache
hints: Conceptual: estimates are deliberately pessimistic, so round up, never down. And a boundary rule like 'strictly above' or 'largest unit whose value is >= 1' has to be read literally: write the boundary cases down before you code.

Specific: math.ceil(x) rounds up and leaves whole numbers alone. For human_bytes, start with n / 1000 and keep dividing by 1000 while the value is still >= 1000 and there's a bigger unit left. Format with f'{value:.1f} {unit}'.

Implementation: validate first and raise ValueError. rps: avg = requests_per_day / SECONDS_PER_DAY; return math.ceil(avg), math.ceil(avg * peak_factor). needs_cache is one comparison: peak_read_rps > db_read_capacity_rps * headroom.
evaluation: No unit beyond TB, and no float formatting for plain bytes
